title: Domī labōrō
summary: Working from home: getting up late, the kids after school, a client meeting tomorrow. Home or the city: which is better? Quotes: Festīnā lentē (Augustus), Venīte ad mē omnēs quī labōrātis (Matthew 11:28), Carpe diem (Horace, Odes 1.11).

intro.en: Today, let's talk about working from home.

lines.en: Hi Marcus. How was your day?
lines.la: Salvē, Marce. Quōmodo fuit diēs tuus?

lines.en: Good, thanks. I worked at home today.
lines.la: Bonus, grātiās. Hodiē domī labōrāvī.

lines.en: At home again? Not in the city?
lines.la: Iterum domī? Nōn in urbe?

lines.en: No. I prefer working at home.
lines.la: Minimē. Domī labōrāre mālō.

lines.en: I work near my family. I like that.
lines.la: Prope familiam meam labōrō. Hoc mihi placet.

lines.en: What time did you get up?
lines.la: Quandō surrēxistī?

lines.en: Late, honestly. At eight.
lines.la: Sērō, vērē. Hōrā octāvā.

lines.en: In the city I have to get up at six.
lines.la: In urbe hōrā sextā surgere dēbeō.

lines.en: So you sleep two hours longer.
lines.la: Ergō duābus hōrīs diūtius dormīs.

lines.en: Exactly. That's why I work at home.
lines.la: Ita. Ideō domī labōrō.

lines.en: And the kids? Weren't they at school?
lines.la: Et līberī? Nōnne in lūdō erant?

lines.en: Yes, they were at school until three.
lines.la: Ita, in lūdō erant ūsque ad hōram tertiam.

lines.en: Then they came home, and I saw them.
lines.la: Deinde domum rediērunt, et eōs vīdī.

lines.en: I was glad, because I like seeing my family.
lines.la: Gāvīsus sum, quia familiam meam vidēre mihi placet.

lines.en: That's nice. In the city, you wouldn't see them.
lines.la: Pulchrum est. In urbe eōs nōn vidērēs.

lines.en: No. I'd get home at seven. Tired.
lines.la: Minimē. Hōrā septimā domum redīrem. Fessus.

lines.en: What are you doing at work this week?
lines.la: Quid hāc hebdomade in labōre agis?

lines.en: I'm making a game for a client. A big project.
lines.la: Lūdum prō cliente faciō. Magnum inceptum.

lines.en: Tomorrow I have a meeting with the client.
lines.la: Crās conventum cum cliente habeō.

lines.en: Are you ready?
lines.la: Parātusne es?

lines.en: Almost. I still have a lot of work.
lines.la: Paene. Adhūc multum labōris habeō.

lines.en: And so… I have to hurry.
lines.la: Itaque… festīnāre dēbeō.

lines.en: Make haste slowly, Marcus.
lines.la: Festīnā lentē, Marce.

lines.en: Make haste slowly… who said that? I can't remember.
lines.la: Festīnā lentē… quis hoc dīxit? Nōn meminī.

lines.en: The emperor Augustus. He said it often.
lines.la: Imperātor Augustus. Hoc saepe dīcēbat.

lines.en: That is: work quickly, but carefully.
lines.la: Id est: celeriter labōrā, sed cum cūrā.

lines.en: Good advice. For an emperor, and for me.
lines.la: Bonum cōnsilium. Imperātōrī, et mihi.

lines.en: Can I ask you something? Home or the city: which is better?
lines.la: Licetne rogāre? Domus an urbs: utra melior est?

lines.en: Hmm… good question.
lines.la: Hmm… bona quaestiō.

lines.en: At home I work alone, and it's quiet.
lines.la: Domī sōlus et tranquillē labōrō.

lines.en: But sometimes I'm too alone. I don't talk to anyone.
lines.la: Sed interdum nimis sōlus sum. Cum nūllō loquor.

lines.en: And in the city?
lines.la: Et in urbe?

lines.en: In the city I see my colleagues. We talk, we laugh.
lines.la: In urbe collēgās meōs videō. Loquimur, rīdēmus.

lines.en: But the trip takes an hour. Every day.
lines.la: Sed iter hōram postulat. Cotīdiē.

lines.en: So for you, home is better?
lines.la: Ergō tibi domus melior est?

lines.en: Yes, I think so. But not every day.
lines.la: Ita putō. Sed nōn omnī diē.

lines.en: Two days in the city, three at home. That's my plan.
lines.la: Duōs diēs in urbe, trēs domī. Hoc est cōnsilium meum.

lines.en: A wise plan.
lines.la: Cōnsilium sapiēns.

lines.en: And this evening? What will you do?
lines.la: Et hodiē vesperī? Quid faciēs?

lines.en: I'm very tired. I'll sit with my wife.
lines.la: Valdē fessus sum. Cum uxōre meā sedēbō.

lines.en: Maybe we'll drink a little wine.
lines.la: Fortasse paulum vīnī bibēmus.

lines.en: You've earned it. Do you know what Jesus says?
lines.la: Hoc meruistī. Scīsne quid Iēsus dīcit?

lines.en: Come to me, all you who labour, and I will refresh you.
lines.la: Venīte ad mē omnēs quī labōrātis, et ego reficiam vōs.

lines.en: Is that from the Gospel of Matthew?
lines.la: Estne ex Ēvangeliō Matthaeī?

lines.en: Yes, chapter eleven. Reficiam: that is, I will give you strength again.
lines.la: Ita, capite ūndecimō. Reficiam: id est, vīrēs vōbīs reddam.

lines.en: I like that. Today I really need it.
lines.la: Hoc mihi placet. Hodiē hōc maximē egeō.

lines.en: And tomorrow, the meeting. Seize the day!
lines.la: Et crās, conventus. Carpe diem!

lines.en: Carpe diem… Horace wrote that?
lines.la: Carpe diem… Horātius hoc scrīpsit?

lines.en: Yes, in his Odes. Use this day well; don't trust tomorrow.
lines.la: Ita, in Carminibus. Hōc diē bene ūtere; nōlī crāstinō crēdere.

lines.en: Don't trust tomorrow… but I have a meeting tomorrow!
lines.la: Nōlī crāstinō crēdere… sed crās conventum habeō!

lines.en: Then carpe diem: finish your work today.
lines.la: Ergō carpe diem: hodiē opus tuum fīnī.

lines.en: Fine. I'll finish it today. Goodbye, Iulia!
lines.la: Bene. Hodiē id fīniam. Valē, Iūlia!

lines.en: Goodbye, Marcus. Good luck tomorrow!
lines.la: Valē, Marce. Crās tibi bona fortūna sit!
